newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Cuba calls UN meet over alleged US bio-attack.
newsitem.headline: Cuba calls UN meet over alleged US bio-attack.

text.p: Signatories of a ban on biological weapons meet in Geneva at Cuba's request this month to examine Havana's charge that the United States dumped a crop pest on the island last year, a brief U.N. statement said on Friday.
Cuba sought the meeting, which will take place on August 25, in a note handed to Russia as depositary of the 1972 Biological Weapons Convention banning deployment and use of biological weapons.
The U.N. statement gave no further details.
Under the 1972 convention, a country that has been a victim of a biological attack may request a consultative meeting of its parties to investigate.

Cuba has said a U.S. government crop duster used in anti-narcotics operations last October sprayed a substance over western Cuba that led to the appearance on the island two months later of Thrips Palmi, a bug that damages many crops.

Washington has denied the accusations. The State Department has acknowledged an S2R crop-duster plane flew over western Cuba during a flight from Florida to the Cayman Islands last October, but said it emitted only smoke to identify its position to a passing Cuban commercial airliner.

President Fidel Castro's government, which has accused the United States in the past of biological warfare, first denounced the latest alleged attack in May. It reiterated the charge at a special U.N. General Assembly meeting on the environment in June.
The charge is the latest spat in long hostile relations between Havana and Washington, which have no diplomatic ties.

The United States maintains a 35-year-old economic embargo on Cuba and is the most aggressive advocate of political change in the hemisphere's only communist nation. Havana views Washington as bent on stripping Cuba of its independence.
